question:
In Quantization for Serving, what failure mode triggers the following observed symptom?
"Edge case trigger: 'Root Cause'"

options.text: Uncoalesced bit-unpacking logic causes high register pressure ($> 64$ registers per thread), forcing register spills into local GPU DRAM.
The dequantization kernel casts INT4 codes to FP32 before unpacking bits and casts back to FP16 afterward, tripling memory traffic per element versus unpacking directly.
dequantize() forgets to subtract zero_point after rescaling, so every value comes out shifted by a constant amount rather than costing extra time.
The kernel launches one thread block per row of the weight matrix regardless of matrix size, leaving most streaming multiprocessors idle on small matrices.

explanation: Diagnostic Analysis: Uncoalesced bit-unpacking logic causes high register pressure ($> 64$ registers per thread), forcing register spills into local GPU DRAM.

Subtract zero_point from each code before multiplying by scale during dequantization.
Switch from per-tensor to per-channel quantization scales to reduce accuracy loss from outlier weights.
Fall back to running the model in FP16 whenever batch size exceeds a fixed threshold.

explanation: Diagnostic Analysis: Use optimized assembly-level packed GEMM kernels (like Marlin or GPTQ-Triton).
